modules.doc:
The fixture package's root module. It depends on [shelf] and
documents one item of its own.

items.name: total_width
items.doc:
The whole shelf's width, given a slot count. Undocumented items
exist in this fixture too — `stack_of` below is one, deliberately,
so the coverage report has something to name.

```wolf
use shelf
shelf.slot_of(1) == 2
```
items.summary: The whole shelf's width, given a slot count.

modules.doc:
A shelf of numbered slots — the s53 documentation fixture.

This module exists to be *documented*, so it exercises every part of
the doc surface at once: a module `//!` block with prose and a
doctest, `///` comments with summary sentences, an intra-doc link to
[slot_of], every fence directive, and a `pub(pkg)` item that a
default run publishes and a `--private` run joins with the private
one below.

```wolf
shelf.slot_of(3) == 4
```
modules.summary: A shelf of numbered slots — the s53 documentation fixture.

items.name: is_slot
items.doc:
Whether a slot number is one a shelf could have.

Passing a string where an `int` belongs is refused, and this fence
asserts the refusal rather than describing it:

```wolf,should_fail(E0401)
shelf.is_slot("three")
```
items.summary: Whether a slot number is one a shelf could have.

items.name: label
items.doc:
The label a shelf prints. The fence here is prose in a fence — a
shape, not a program — so it carries `ignore`.

```wolf,ignore
<slot>: <title> (<width>)
```

items.name: rows
items.doc:
A package-visible helper: `pub(pkg)` is published surface inside the
package and invisible outside it, and the page says which.

```wolf
shelf.rows(2) == 2
```
items.summary: A package-visible helper: `pub(pkg)` is published surface inside the package and invisible outside it, and the page says which.

items.name: slot_of
items.doc:
The slot a book of width `w` occupies. The first sentence ends
here, and everything after it is the body — which is how a listing
can be one line while a page is a page.

A shelf is one-indexed, so the answer is always at least 1. See
[width_of] for the inverse, and [shelf.slot_of] for this same
function named the long way.

```wolf
shelf.slot_of(0) == 1
shelf.slot_of(7) == 8
```
items.summary: The slot a book of width `w` occupies.

items.name: width_of
items.doc:
The width a slot holds — the inverse of [slot_of].

The fence below is compiled and never executed: it demonstrates the
shape of a call whose value nobody wants.

```wolf,no_run
let w = shelf.width_of(9)
```
items.summary: The width a slot holds — the inverse of [slot_of].
